facts.text: Bonneville Crater was deployed at Gusev Crater during Spirit (MER-A) in 2004.

Bonneville Crater was one of Spirit's first major waypoints, a 200-metre impact crater about 300 metres from the landing site. Scientists hoped to find exposed rock layers in its walls, but found mostly loose soil. The disappointment led to the decision to drive the 3 km to Columbia Hills — which turned out to be the right call.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Showed that not all craters expose useful rock layers, which redirected the mission toward the far more rewarding Columbia Hills.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Gusev Crater.
Bonneville Crater remains an unremarkable impact feature, but it played a pivotal role in the decision that made the Spirit mission legendary.
